In Technological Design, the fabricated object is evidence inside a design process. Require a defensible brief, criteria and constraints, alternative concepts, measured drawings or CAD, prototype testing, and a revision—not just a rendered final form.

## Project directions

:::: {.ter-project-grid}
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Ergonomic shared-tool organizer
<p class="ter-course-code">TDJ2O / senior TDJ · Organizer family</p>
Improve access for two users with different reach, hand size, or visual needs while keeping an accurate inventory visible.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Observation → anthropometric assumptions → mock-up → parametric CAD → prototype</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Criteria weighting, ergonomics, clearances, technical drawing, user testing</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate · desktop module under 350 mm wide</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Cardboard proof, then plywood or printed polymer components</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Test tipping, handle load, repeated removal, and replaceable parts</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Do not infer accessibility from one user; remove pinch and sharp-edge hazards</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=technological-design&type=french-cleat">Modular organization interfaces</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../01-nice-design-process/04-prototype-evaluate-iterate.qmd">Prototype, Evaluate & Iterate</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Publish a parameter table that allows another class to resize the design</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Comparative fit-test fixture
<p class="ter-course-code">TDJ2O / senior TDJ · Gauge family</p>
Create a fixture that isolates one variable—clearance, slot fit, fastener position, or printed tolerance—and records repeatable results.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Define variable → control geometry → fabricate series → measure → graph result</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Experimental design, tolerancing, data visualization, revision control</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate · hand-sized coupon series</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>The same stock or filament planned for the final prototype</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Include datums and labels that survive handling</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Test samples are process references, not rated structural coupons</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=technological-design&type=calibration">Calibration assets</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../03-laser-cutting/04-material-fit-calibration.qmd">Material Fit + Calibration</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Compare two machines or orientations and explain the different result</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Configurable product display
<p class="ter-course-code">Senior TDJ · Display family</p>
Design a knock-down display whose angle, message panel, or product support can change without remaking the whole system.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Use scenario → mechanism concepts → scale model → full-size critical joint</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Systems thinking, interfaces, assembly sequence, communication drawing</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate–advanced · 300–600 mm tall</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Sheet stock plus printed connectors or standard fasteners</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>State load case, safety factor assumption, and failure mode</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Prototype displays only; public installation requires appropriate review</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=technological-design&type=project-components">Project components</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../03-laser-cutting/05-assemblies-hybrid-fabrication.qmd">Assemblies + Hybrid Fabrication</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Prepare an exploded view, bill of materials, and end-of-life plan</dd></dl>
:::
::::

## What makes the work TDJ

The technology area is visible in decisions: who the design serves, how requirements are ranked, why a model is valid, which test produces useful evidence, and how feedback changes the proposal. CAD quality matters, but it does not replace inquiry or evaluation.

::: {.ter-curriculum-relevance}
**Curriculum context:** Use these directions to support design-process, communication, modelling, technical drawing, material/process selection, evaluation, and career-learning expectations appropriate to the current TDJ course.
:::
